newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-49ERS SIGN FREE AGENT RB GARRISON HEARST.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-49ERS SIGN FREE AGENT RB GARRISON HEARST.

text.p: The San Francisco 49ers Friday signed unrestricted free agent running back Garrison Hearst, who had been with the Cincinnati Bengals, to a two-year contract.

"The bottom line was that I've played for two teams that hadn't done that well," Hearst said at a news conference to announce his signing. "Now I have a chance to go out there and play some playoff games.
"I'm very happy with what I received and I'll be even happier when we go back to the Super Bowl," he said.
Hearst, 26, the third overall pick in the 1993 draft, was a 1,000-yard rusher for the Arizona Cardinals in 1995.
He is the second free agent signed by the Niners in the off-season. San Francisco signed offensive lineman Kevin Gogan from the Oakland Raiders last month.
Hearst played in only 14 of 32 games his first two seasons with Arizona due to knee problems. In an injury-free 1995 season he rushed for 1,070 yards on 284 carries.
But the Cardinals asked Hearst to take a drastic pay cut last year, and when no agreement was reached he was waived by Arizona and picked up by the Bengals.
Hearst, who will challenge Terry Kirby for the starting halfback spot on the Niners, led Cincinnati in rushing last season with 847 yards on 225 carries.

"Garrison gives us another tailback who is very quick, very fast, has the ability to go the distance, (and) has the ability to catch the ball out of the backfield and do some real damage," said new Niners coach Steve Mariucci.
